message.content: In lions, one of the most striking dominant traits is the **presence of a functional melanocortin‑1 receptor (MC1R) allele** that drives the production of eumelanin (black pigment). This allele is responsible for the characteristic dark fur and, in males, the development of a full mane. Because it is dominant, a single copy of the allele is enough to produce the black coloration and mane growth seen in most adult lions.
